questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding the Planning Commission?
I. It was established in 1952.
II. The President of India was its chairperson.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Planning Commission** was established by an executive resolution of the **Government of India** on **March 15, 1950**. It was not established in **1952**, although the **First Five-Year Plan** was launched in 1951. **Hence, statement I is incorrect.**
 
• The internal hierarchy of the **Planning Commission** mandated that the **Prime Minister of India** serve as the **ex-officio Chairperson**. The **President of India** had no formal role in the leadership or day-to-day operations of the commission. **Hence, statement II is incorrect.**
 
• The body was created following the recommendations of the **Advisory Planning Board**, which had been set up in 1946 under the chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**.
 
• Its primary mandate was to formulate **Five-Year Plans** for the most effective and balanced utilization of the country's material, capital, and human **resources**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution and Dissolution:**
 
 
• The **Planning Commission** was a **non-constitutional** and **non-statutory** body, meaning it was not created by the **Constitution** or an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• On **August 13, 2014**, the **Government of India** scrapped the commission to make way for a more contemporary structure.
 
• It was officially replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) on **January 1, 2015**, which emphasizes **cooperative federalism**.
 
• The first **Deputy Chairperson** of the Planning Commission was **Gulzarilal Nanda**, while the last Deputy Chairperson was **Montek Singh Ahluwalia**.
 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** was the body responsible for giving final approval to the **Five-Year Plans** formulated by the commission.

questions.question: Lakshadweep Islands are located in the ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arabian Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lakshadweep** is India's smallest **Union Territory** and is an archipelago consisting of **36 islands** located in the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The total land area of the territory is approximately **32 square kilometers**, and it is located about **200 to 440 kilometers** off the **Malabar Coast** of **Kerala**.
 
• The islands are of **coral origin** and are classified as **atolls**, which are circular coral reefs that partially or completely enclose a lagoon.
 
• The administrative headquarters of **Lakshadweep** is located on the island of **Kavaratti**.
 
• The islands were originally known as the **Laccadive, Minicoy, and Amindivi Islands** until they were renamed **Lakshadweep** by an act of Parliament in **1973**.
 
• Only **10 islands** out of the 36 are inhabited, including **Agatti**, **Amini**, **Andrott**, **Bitra**, **Chetlat**, **Kadmat**, **Kalpeni**, **Kavaratti**, **Kiltan**, and **Minicoy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay of Bengal**:

 
 
• Located to the east of the Indian peninsula, it houses the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, which are **volcanic** in origin and represent the elevated portions of submerged mountain ranges.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Channels**:
 
 
• The **8 Degree Channel** separates the island of **Minicoy** (India) from the **Maldives**.
 
• The **9 Degree Channel** separates **Minicoy** from the main **Lakshadweep** archipelago.
 
• The **10 Degree Channel** separates the **Andaman Islands** from the **Nicobar Islands** in the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Ecology**:
 
 
• **Pitti Island** is an important site in the region as it serves as a **Bird Sanctuary** and is uninhabited by humans.
 
• The region is governed by an **Administrator** appointed by the **President of India** under **Article 239** of the Constitution.

questions.question: Megasthenes visited the court of Chandragupta Maurya as an ambassador sent by ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seleucus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megasthenes** was an ancient **Greek historian**, diplomat, and explorer who served as a **Hellenistic ambassador** to India during the 4th century BCE.
 
• He was dispatched to the court of **Chandragupta Maurya** by **Seleucus I Nicator**, the founder of the **Seleucid Empire** and one of the most powerful generals of **Alexander the Great**.
 
• The appointment of **Megasthenes** followed a peace treaty between **Seleucus I** and **Chandragupta Maurya** around **305 BCE**, which concluded their conflict over the **Indus Valley** territories.
 
• He resided in the **Mauryan capital** of **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna) for several years, providing a detailed Western perspective on the **Mauryan administration** and Indian life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indica:**

 
 
• This is the title of the seminal book written by **Megasthenes**. Although the original text is lost, its contents are known through citations by later classical authors such as **Arrian**, **Strabo**, and **Pliny**.
 
• The book categorized Indian society into **seven classes** and described the absence of slavery in India, though modern historians suggest this was a misinterpretation of the **Shudra** status or debt bondage.
 
 
 
• **Seleucus I Nicator:**
 
 
• After the death of **Alexander** in **323 BCE**, he secured the eastern satrapies of the empire.
 
• In the settlement with **Chandragupta Maurya**, he received **500 war elephants**, which proved decisive in his victory at the **Battle of Ipsus** in 301 BCE.
 
 
 
• **Alexander the Great:**
 
 
• He invaded India in **326 BCE**, crossing the **Indus River** and fighting King **Porus** at the **Battle of the Hydaspes**, but his troops mutinied at the **Beas River**, forcing his retreat.
 
 
 
• **Harshvardhan:**
 
 
• He was a ruler of the **Pushyabhuti dynasty** who reigned much later, from **606 to 647 CE**. His court was visited by the famous Chinese traveler **Xuanzang**.

questions.question: Oxygen-rich blood from the lungs enters which of the following chamber of heart in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Left atrium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human heart is a **muscular organ** divided into four chambers: two upper **atria** and two lower **ventricles**, designed to prevent the mixing of **oxygenated** and **deoxygenated blood**.
 
• The process of **oxygenation** occurs in the **lungs**, where **carbon dioxide** is removed from the blood and **oxygen** is absorbed through the **alveolar-capillary membrane**.
 
• Once the blood becomes **oxygen-rich**, it travels from the **lungs** to the heart via the **pulmonary veins**; humans typically have four pulmonary veins.
 
• The **left atrium** is the specific chamber that receives this **oxygenated blood**, serving as a primary receiving station before the blood moves into the **systemic circulation**.
 
• From the left atrium, the blood passes through the **mitral valve** (also known as the **bicuspid valve**) into the **left ventricle**, which then pumps it to the rest of the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right Atrium**

 
 
• Function: Receives **deoxygenated blood** returning from the body tissues.
 
• Vessels: Blood enters via the **Superior Vena Cava** (from the upper body) and the **Inferior Vena Cava** (from the lower body).
 
 
 
• **Right Ventricle**
 
 
• Function: Pumps the **deoxygenated blood** to the **lungs** for purification.
 
• Vessel: Blood is ejected through the **pulmonary valve** into the **pulmonary artery**.
 
 
 
• **Left Ventricle**
 
 
• Function: Responsible for pumping **oxygen-rich blood** to every organ and tissue in the body.
 
• Structure: It has the **thickest myocardium** (muscle wall) among all chambers to generate the high **blood pressure** needed for **systemic circulation** through the **aorta**.

questions.question: Which of the following component of blood stops bleeding?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blood platelets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood platelets**, scientifically referred to as **thrombocytes**, are small, disc-shaped, colorless cell fragments that lack a nucleus and are essential for the process of **hemostasis**.
 
• They are produced in the **bone marrow** through the fragmentation of extremely large cells called **megakaryocytes**; a healthy adult typically maintains a platelet count ranging from **150,000 to 450,000** platelets per microliter of blood.
 
• When a blood vessel is injured, platelets undergo a three-step process: **adhesion** to the damaged site, **activation** to change shape and release chemical signals, and **aggregation** to form a physical barrier known as a **platelet plug**.
 
• Platelets facilitate the **blood clotting cascade** by releasing **thromboplastin**, which helps convert the soluble protein **fibrinogen** into insoluble **fibrin** strands, creating a mesh that stabilizes the clot and prevents further blood loss.
 
• The average lifespan of a platelet in the circulatory system is approximately **8 to 10 days**, after which they are filtered out and destroyed primarily by the **spleen**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red blood cells (Erythrocytes)**:

 
 
• Contain the iron-containing protein **hemoglobin**, which is responsible for transporting **oxygen** from the lungs to tissues and **carbon dioxide** back to the lungs.
 
• They have a distinct **biconcave shape** to increase surface area for gas exchange and lack most organelles, including a nucleus, to maximize space for hemoglobin.
 
 
 
• **White blood cells (Leukocytes)**:
 
 
• Act as the primary components of the **immune system**, defending the body against pathogens, viruses, and foreign materials.
 
• They are categorized into **granulocytes** (neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils) and **agranulocytes** (lymphocytes, monocytes), each serving specialized defensive roles.
 
 
 
• **Plasma**:
 
 
• The straw-colored liquid component of blood that makes up about **55 percent** of the total blood volume.
 
• It consists of about **90-92 percent water** and carries vital substances such as **electrolytes**, **hormones**, **nutrients**, and **plasma proteins** like albumin and globulin.

questions.question: The President of India can be impeached for violation of the Indian Constitution under which Article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 61**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 61** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the detailed procedure for the **impeachment** of the **President of India**.
 
• The **President** can be removed from office before the expiry of their term only on the grounds of **'violation of the Constitution'**.
 
• The impeachment process is a **quasi-judicial procedure** that can be initiated in either House of Parliament—the **Lok Sabha** or the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• To initiate the process, a **14-day written notice** must be given to the President, which must be signed by at least **one-fourth** of the total members of the House in which the charges are originated.
 
• The resolution for impeachment must be passed by a **special majority**, which is not less than **two-thirds of the total membership** of the initiating House.
 
• Once passed, the other House **investigates the charges**, during which the President has the **right to appear** and be represented. If the second House also passes the resolution by a **two-thirds majority** of the total membership, the President stands removed from the date the resolution is passed.
 
• Statistically, to date, **no President** of India has ever been impeached.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 60**:

 
 
• This article deals with the **Oath or Affirmation** of the President.
 
• The oath is administered by the **Chief Justice of India** or, in their absence, the **senior-most Judge** of the **Supreme Court**.
 
 
 
• **Article 55**:
 
 
• Specifies the **manner of election** of the President of India.
 
• The election is held through a **secret ballot** using the system of **proportional representation** by means of a **single transferable vote**.
 
 
 
• **Article 63**:
 
 
• States that there shall be a **Vice-President of India**.
 
• The Vice-President acts as the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha** as per **Article 64**.

questions.question: What is Death rate?

options.text: It is the number of deaths per 100 people.
It is the number of deaths per 1000 people.
It is the number of deaths per 10000 people.
It is the number of deaths per 100000 people.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the number of deaths per 1000 people**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Death Rate**, technically referred to as the **Crude Death Rate (CDR)**, is a primary demographic measure representing the number of deaths occurring in a specific population during a given period.
 
• It is conventionally expressed as the number of deaths per **1,000 individuals** in the population per year.
 
• The rate is calculated by taking the **total number of deaths** in a year, dividing it by the **mid-year total population** of that year, and multiplying the result by **1,000**.
 
• This metric allows for the comparison of mortality levels across different geographical regions or time periods, standardizing the data against population size.
 
• In **India**, the **Sample Registration System (SRS)** is the primary source of data for estimating the annual death rate at both state and national levels.
 
• According to global statistics, mortality rates are influenced by factors such as **healthcare accessibility**, **sanitation**, **nutritional standards**, and the **age structure** of the population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Demographic Metrics**:

 
 
• **Birth Rate**: This is the counterpart to the death rate, measured as the number of **live births per 1,000 people** in a year.
 
• **Natural Increase**: This is the difference between the **Birth Rate** and the **Death Rate**; it indicates the speed at which a population grows naturally, excluding migration.
 
• **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)**: This measures the deaths of children under **one year of age** per **1,000 live births**, serving as a critical indicator of a country’s overall health status.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Scale**:
 
 
• While general death rates use a base of **1,000**, certain specialized metrics use different scales. For instance, the **Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)** is calculated per **100,000 live births** to provide a more precise measure of rare events.
 
• Tracking death rates is essential for **public health planning**, **epidemiological studies**, and the formulation of **social welfare policies**.

questions.question:
According to the new system of justice established by the British in 1772, which of the following courts was to be there in every district?

I. Faujdari adalat

II. Diwani adalat
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1772**, the **British East India Company** under **Warren Hastings** introduced a new system of justice to streamline the administration in **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Orissa**. Under this plan, each district was required to have two types of courts.
 
• The **Faujdari adalat** served as the **Criminal Court** in every district. While it was presided over by a **Qazi** and a **Mufti** (assisted by **Maulvis**), it remained under the overall supervision of the **European District Collector** to ensure transparency. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• The **Diwani adalat** served as the **Civil Court** in every district. These courts were established to handle matters related to **land revenue**, **property**, and **family disputes**. They were directly presided over by the **Collector** of the district. **Hence, statement II is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Warren Hastings**:

 
 
• He was the first **Governor-General of Bengal** (1773−1785) and played a crucial role in centralizing **British administration**.
 
• He abolished the **Dual System of Government** and took direct responsibility for **Revenue Collection** and **Judicial Administration**.
 
 
 
• **Appellate Courts**:
 
 
• Beyond the district level, two superior courts were established in **Calcutta**: the **Sadar Diwani Adalat** (for civil appeals) and the **Sadar Nizamat Adalat** (for criminal appeals).
 
• In the **Diwani** courts, the **Collector** was assisted by **Hindu Pandits** and **Muslim Maulvis** to interpret local religious laws and customs before delivering a judgment.
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** later led to the establishment of the **Supreme Court at Calcutta** in 1774.

questions.question: The International Space Station orbit the earth approximately ______ times a day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** travels at an average speed of approximately **28,000 kilometers per hour** (about **17,500 miles per hour**).
 
• Due to this immense velocity, the station completes one full revolution around the **Earth** in approximately **90 to 93 minutes**.
 
• Since there are **1,440 minutes** in a standard **24-hour day**, dividing this by the **90-minute** orbital period results in approximately **16 orbits** per day.
 
• This orbital frequency means that the astronauts and cosmonauts living on the station witness **16 sunrises** and **16 sunsets** every day.
 
• The **ISS** maintains a **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)** at an average altitude of about **400 kilometers** (roughly **250 miles**) above the Earth's surface.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Orbital Mechanics and Features**:

 
 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO)**: This is the orbital range within **2,000 kilometers** of the planet's surface, where most **artificial satellites** and **manned missions** operate.
 
• **Orbital Inclination**: The **ISS** is positioned at an inclination of **51.6 degrees** relative to the equator, which allows it to cover over **90 percent** of the Earth's inhabited population.
 
• **International Partnership**: The station is a joint venture between **NASA** (United States), **Roscosmos** (Russia), **JAXA** (Japan), **ESA** (Europe), and **CSA** (Canada).
 
• **Microgravity Environment**: The primary purpose of the **ISS** is to serve as a research laboratory for **astrobiology**, **materials science**, and **meteorology** under near-weightless conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following movement was re-launched in 1932?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Civil Disobedience Movement**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Civil Disobedience Movement** was first launched by **Mahatma Gandhi** on **12 March 1930**, with the famous **Dandi March** to break the salt law.
 
• Following the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** signed in **March 1931**, the movement was suspended, and **Mahatma Gandhi** agreed to participate in the **Second Round Table Conference** in **London**.
 
• The conference failed to yield any concrete results regarding **India's independence** or constitutional reforms, leading to Gandhi's return to India in **December 1931**.
 
• Upon his return, Gandhi found that the British government, under **Viceroy Lord Willingdon**, had adopted a policy of severe repression, arresting leaders like **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**.
 
• The **Indian National Congress** was declared an illegal organization, and its offices were seized by the colonial authorities.
 
• In response to this hostility and the failure of diplomatic talks, the movement was officially re-launched in **January 1932**.
 
• The second phase of the movement continued with varying intensity until it was officially withdrawn in **May 1934** due to declining momentum and government crackdowns.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**:
 
 
• Launched in **1920**, it aimed at obtaining **Swaraj** (Self-rule) through non-violent means and the boycott of British institutions.
 
• It was abruptly called off by Gandhi in **February 1922** after the **Chauri Chaura** incident, where a violent mob set fire to a police station.
 
 
 
• **Khilafat Movement**:
 
 
• Started around **1919** by the **Ali Brothers** (**Mohammad Ali** and **Shaukat Ali**) to protest the dismantling of the **Ottoman Caliphate** after **World War I**.
 
• It merged with the **Non-Cooperation Movement** to forge **Hindu-Muslim unity** against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Bardoli Satyagraha**:
 
 
• A major peasant movement in **1928** in **Gujarat** led by **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**.
 
• It was a successful protest against the **30 percent** increase in land revenue, which earned Patel the title of **Sardar**.

questions.question: As of July 2025, India has about ____ lakh Elected Women Representatives (EWRs) in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14.5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India currently boasts approximately **14.5 lakh** Elected Women Representatives (EWRs) within its **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**, reflecting a massive transformation in rural leadership.
 
• Out of the nearly **31.87 lakh** total elected representatives across the three tiers of Panchayats (Gram, Block, and District), women now constitute about **46 percent** of the leadership.
 
• This substantial figure of **14.5 lakh** indicates that women have moved beyond the minimum statutory requirements, winning seats in both **reserved** and **general categories**.
 
• The high representation at the grassroots level underscores India's commitment to **women-led development** and gender-inclusive policy-making in local governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**:
 
 
• This act accorded constitutional status to **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and introduced **Part IX** to the Constitution of India.
 
• **Article 243D**: It specifically mandates the reservation of not less than **one-third (33.3%)** of the total number of seats and offices of chairpersons for women.
 
• **State Initiatives**: More than **20 states**, including **Bihar**, **Uttarakhand**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Rajasthan**, have legally increased the reservation for women in PRIs to **50 percent**.
 
• **Three-Tier System**: The structure comprises the **Gram Panchayat** at the village level, **Panchayat Samiti** at the intermediate level, and **Zila Parishad** at the district level.
 
• **Social Impact**: The presence of **Elected Women Representatives** has led to increased focus on **maternal health**, **sanitation**, **drinking water**, and **primary education** in rural areas.

questions.question: ____ is the second most used metal in the world after steel.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aluminum** is officially recognized as the **second most used metal** in the world, following **steel** (iron). Its versatility across various industrial sectors makes it the most consumed **non-ferrous metal** globally.
 
• The metal is prized for its **low density**, which is approximately one-third that of steel or copper, making it essential for industries where **weight reduction** is critical without sacrificing structural integrity.
 
• The primary source of aluminum is **Bauxite ore**. The extraction process involves the **Bayer Process** to produce alumina (aluminum oxide) and the **Hall-Héroult Process** to smelt the alumina into pure aluminum through **electrolysis**.
 
• Its **corrosion resistance** is a result of a thin, naturally occurring layer of **aluminum oxide** that forms on the surface when exposed to air, protecting the underlying metal from further oxidation.
 
• Global production and consumption of aluminum have surged due to its **high recyclability**; nearly 75 percent of all aluminum ever produced is still in use today, requiring significantly less energy to recycle than to produce from raw ore.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Applications of Aluminum**

 
 
• **Aerospace and Transport**: Utilized in **aircraft frames**, automotive engine components, and high-speed rail bodies due to its **high strength-to-weight ratio**.
 
• **Packaging**: Dominates the **beverage can** and foil markets because it is non-toxic and provides an excellent barrier against light and oxygen.
 
• **Electrical**: Used in **long-distance power transmission** lines because it is more cost-effective and lighter than copper for the same level of conductivity.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Metals**
 
 
• **Zinc**: Primarily used as a **protective coating** for steel in a process known as **galvanization** to prevent rusting.
 
• **Nickel**: A critical alloying element used mainly in the production of **stainless steel** and increasingly in **lithium-ion batteries** for electric vehicles.
 
• **Lead**: Characterized by its high density and low melting point, used predominantly in **lead-acid batteries** and radiation shielding.

questions.question: What is deducted from Gross domestic product (GDP) at market prices to calculate GDP at factor cost?

options.text: Only subsidy provided by the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net product taxes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at Market Price** represents the total market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic boundaries of a country during a specific period, including the impact of **Indirect Taxes** and **Subsidies**.
 
• **GDP at Factor Cost** measures the total cost of all factors of production used to produce goods and services, including **Rent**, **Wages**, **Interest**, and **Profit**, excluding the effect of government interventions like taxes.
 
• The bridge between **Market Price (MP)** and **Factor Cost (FC)** is **Net Indirect Taxes (NIT)**, which is calculated as **Indirect Taxes − Subsidies**.
 
• To convert **GDP at Market Price** to **GDP at Factor Cost**, we must subtract the **Net Indirect Taxes** (often referred to as **Net product taxes** in national accounting) because indirect taxes inflate the market price while subsidies deflate it.
 
• The mathematical relationship is: **GDP at Factor Cost = GDP at Market Price − Net Indirect Taxes** or **GDP at Factor Cost = GDP at Market Price − Indirect Taxes + Subsidies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Depreciation**:

 
 
• Also known as the **Consumption of Fixed Capital**, it is the value deducted from **Gross** aggregates (like GDP) to calculate **Net** aggregates (like **Net Domestic Product** or **NDP**).
 
• It accounts for the physical wear and tear and obsolescence of **fixed assets** over time.
 
 
 
• **National Debt Interest**:
 
 
• This refers to interest payments made by the government on **borrowed funds**. It is treated as a **transfer payment** because it does not involve any current production of goods or services.
 
• It is generally excluded from the calculation of **National Income** and does not factor into the conversion between **Market Price** and **Factor Cost**.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**:
 
 
• These are **financial assistances** provided by the government to producers to lower the market price of essential commodities.
 
• While **Subsidies** are added to **Market Price** to find **Factor Cost**, they are only a component of **Net Indirect Taxes**; deducting only subsidies would not yield the correct **Factor Cost**.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Greatest: My Own Story** is the definitive **autobiography** of the legendary American heavyweight boxing champion **Muhammad Ali**.
 
• Published in **1975**, the memoir was co-written with **Richard Durham**, a prominent journalist and activist who helped capture Ali's unique voice and perspective.
 
• The narrative provides a detailed account of Ali's life, including his **1960 Olympic gold medal**, his conversion to **Islam**, and his refusal to be drafted into the **Vietnam War** on religious grounds.
 
• A significant literary fact is that the book was edited by the Nobel Prize-winning author **Toni Morrison**, who was then a senior editor at **Random House**.

• **Floyd Mayweather**:

questions.question: The word 'Popping' is related to which part of game of cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Popping** refers specifically to the **Popping Crease**, which is the most significant line marked at each end of a **Cricket Pitch**.
 
• As per the **Laws of Cricket** maintained by the **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)**, the popping crease is drawn **4 feet (1.22 meters)** in front of and parallel to the **Bowling Crease**.
 
• For a **Bowler**, the popping crease acts as the front boundary during the delivery stride; if the bowler’s front foot lands entirely beyond this line, it results in a **No-Ball**.
 
• For a **Batsman**, the popping crease defines the limit of their **ground**. A batsman is considered safe from **Stumping** or **Run-out** only if some part of their bat or person is grounded behind this crease.
 
• The line is considered to be of **infinite length**, although it is marked for at least **6 feet** on either side of the center of the pitch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bowling Crease**

 
 
• This is the line through the centers of the three **stumps** at each end.
 
• It measures **8 feet 8 inches (2.64 meters)** in length.
 
 
 
• **Return Crease**
 
 
• These are lines perpendicular to the **popping crease**, marked at a distance of **4 feet 4 inches** from the middle stump.
 
• They prevent the bowler from delivering the ball from an excessively wide angle.
 
 
 
• **30-Yard Circle**
 
 
• Used primarily in **Limited Overs Cricket** (ODIs and T20s) to regulate **Fielding Restrictions** during powerplays.
 
• It distinguishes between the **infield** and the **outfield**.
 
 
 
• **Boundary**
 
 
• The perimeter of the **playing area**, usually marked by a rope or a white line, defining where a **Four** or a **Six** is scored.

questions.question: Who developed the Shalimar Gardens in Lahore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shalimar Gardens** in **Lahore** were commissioned by the **Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan** in **1641 AD** and completed in **1642 AD**.
 
• The construction was managed by **Khalilullah Khan**, a prominent noble of the Mughal court, while the hydraulic systems were designed by **Ali Mardan Khan**.
 
• The garden is built in the **Charbagh** (four-fold garden) layout, which is a hallmark of **Persian-style** Islamic architecture, representing the gardens of **Paradise**.
 
• The site was inscribed as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1981** due to its outstanding universal value in **Mughal garden design** and engineering.
 
• The water supply for the gardens was sourced through the **Shah Nahar** (Royal Canal), which brought water from **Rajpur** (modern-day Madhopur) over a distance of approximately **100 miles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terrace Structure**:

 
 
• The gardens are arranged on three descending terraces: the upper terrace named **Farah Baksh** (Bestower of Pleasure), the middle terrace **Faiz Baksh** (Bestower of Goodness), and the lower terrace **Hayat Baksh** (Bestower of Life).
 
• The layout includes **410 fountains** and numerous white marble **pavilions** (baradaris).
 
 
 
• **Other Mughal Emperors**:
 
 
• **Babur**: The first Mughal emperor who introduced the **Charbagh** concept to the Indian subcontinent with the **Ram Bagh** in Agra.
 
• **Akbar**: Known for synthesizing Persian and Indian styles, building the **Agra Fort** and the planned city of **Fatehpur Sikri**.
 
• **Jahangir**: Shah Jahan's father, who built the original **Shalimar Bagh** in **Srinagar, Kashmir**, in **1619 AD**, which served as the primary inspiration for the Lahore gardens.

questions.question: ______ is a farming system with minimal or no use of chemicals as fertilizers, herbicides, pesticides, etc., and with a maximum input of organic manures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Organic farming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Organic farming** is a holistic agricultural system that emphasizes the use of **organic manures**, **crop rotation**, and **biological pest control** while strictly limiting or excluding synthetic **fertilizers**, **pesticides**, and **herbicides**.
 
• The primary objective of this system is to maintain **soil fertility** and **ecological balance** by utilizing natural inputs like **vermicompost**, **green manure**, and **bio-fertilizers**.
 
• In India, the **National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP)** provides the regulatory framework for organic certification, ensuring that the farming practices avoid **genetically modified organisms (GMOs)** and **chemical residues**.
 
• This method promotes **biodiversity** and **environmental sustainability** by reducing soil erosion and nitrate leaching into groundwater, which are common issues in conventional agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial farming**:

 
 
• Characterized by **large-scale monocultures** and intensive use of **synthetic chemicals** and **machinery**.
 
• Focuses on maximizing **yield** and **economic efficiency** through the use of **chemical growth regulators**.
 
 
 
• **Permaculture**:
 
 
• A design system developed by **Bill Mollison** and **David Holmgren** that integrates **landscape** and **people** through self-maintained agricultural systems.
 
• It goes beyond simple farming to include **water harvesting**, **renewable energy**, and **sustainable architecture**.
 
 
 
• **Ley farming**:
 
 
• A system where **arable crops** are grown in rotation with **seeded pasture** or **grassland** (leys).
 
• The **ley period** helps in restoring **soil structure** and increasing **nitrogen content** naturally through legumes.

questions.question: In Mendeleev's Periodic Table, elements were arranged considering ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**similarity of chemical properties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**, a Russian chemist, formulated the **Periodic Law** in **1869**, which stated that the physical and chemical properties of elements are a periodic function of their **atomic masses**.
 
• While atomic mass was the fundamental physical basis for the arrangement, the primary organizational criterion was the **similarity of chemical properties** among elements.
 
• Mendeleev focused on the **chemical reactivity** of elements, specifically focusing on the **formulas of the hydrides and oxides** formed by them. He treated these chemical formulas as basic properties for classification.
 
• Elements that exhibited similar chemical behavior, such as forming compounds with similar **stoichiometry** and **valency**, were grouped together in the same vertical columns, known as **groups**.
 
• He prioritized chemical similarity so heavily that he occasionally placed an element with a slightly greater atomic mass before one with a lower atomic mass (e.g., **Cobalt** before **Nickel**) to maintain chemical consistency within a group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Mass and Gaps**:

 
 
• Mendeleev arranged the **63 elements** known at the time in increasing order of **atomic weight**.
 
• By relying on chemical trends, he successfully predicted the existence and properties of undiscovered elements, leaving gaps for **Eka-boron** (Scandium), **Eka-aluminium** (Gallium), and **Eka-silicon** (Germanium).
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Modern Table**:
 
 
• The **Modern Periodic Table**, proposed by **Henry Moseley** in **1913**, transitioned the basis of classification from **atomic mass** to **atomic number**.
 
• While Mendeleev used **chemical properties** to guide his mass-based arrangement, modern chemistry confirms that these properties are determined by the **electronic configuration** and **atomic number**.
